# Example Org Authentication & Credential Management Standard

**Document Owner:** IAM Engineering
**Applies to:** All Example Org information systems, users, devices, and processes that authenticate to organizational systems
**Process cadence:** Continuous

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This Standard defines the mandatory requirements for authentication and credential management at Example Org. It governs invalid logon handling, session control, system use notification, identification and authentication of users and devices, authenticator management, authentication feedback, cryptographic module authentication, non-organizational user authentication, and re-authentication. IAM Engineering is accountable for this process end to end, including implementation, review, and evidence production.

## 2. Roles and Responsibilities

- **IAM Engineering** owns this Standard and the authentication and credential management process it defines, including configuration of authentication controls, review of authentication policy settings, and production of the MFA enrolment report and the Authentication policy configuration export.
- **System administrators** participate in account lockout release and authenticator lifecycle actions as specified below.
- **Help desk support** shall require user identification for any transaction with information security and privacy implications.

## 3. Invalid Logon Attempts and Account Lockout

3.1. The organization shall enforce a limit of [Assignment: organization-defined number] consecutive invalid logon attempts by a user during a [Assignment: organization-defined time period]. [NIST AC-7 Low/Moderate/High]

3.2. The limit shall be five (5) consecutive invalid logon attempts by a user during a fifteen (15) minute time period. [ARC-AMPE AC-7 AE Mandatory]

3.3. When the maximum number of unsuccessful attempts is exceeded, the organization shall automatically take one or more of the following: lock the account or node for [Assignment: organization-defined time period]; lock the account or node until released by an administrator; delay the next logon prompt per [Assignment: organization-defined delay algorithm]; notify the system administrator; or take another [Assignment: organization-defined action]. [NIST AC-7 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-7 AE Mandatory]

3.4. When the maximum number of unsuccessful attempts is exceeded, the organization shall automatically lock the account or node for a minimum of thirty (30) minutes, lock it until released by an administrator, delay the next logon prompt consistent with a delay algorithm, notify the system administrator, or take other action as determined by the organization. [ARC-AMPE AC-7 AE Mandatory]

3.5. The organization shall purge or wipe information from [Assignment: organization-defined mobile devices], based on [Assignment: organization-defined purging or wiping requirements and techniques], after [Assignment: organization-defined number] consecutive unsuccessful device logon attempts. [NIST AC-7(2)]

3.6. Mobile devices shall be configured to purge or wipe information after ten (10) consecutive unsuccessful logon attempts. [ARC-AMPE AC-7 AE Mandatory]

3.7. The organization shall limit the number of unsuccessful biometric logon attempts to [Assignment: organization-defined number]. [NIST AC-7(3)]

3.8. After the organization-defined number of consecutive invalid logon attempts is exceeded, the organization shall allow the use of [Assignment: organization-defined authentication factors] different from the primary authentication factors, and shall enforce a limit of [Assignment: organization-defined number] consecutive invalid logon attempts through use of those alternative factors by a user during a [Assignment: organization-defined time period]. [NIST AC-7(4)]

IAM Engineering shall monitor lockout enforcement through the [Identity Provider] on a continuous basis.

## 4. System Use Notification

4.1. The organization shall display [Assignment: organization-defined system use notification] to users before granting access to the system, providing privacy and security notices consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines. [NIST AC-8 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-8 AE Mandatory]

4.2. The system use notification shall state that: system usage may be monitored, recorded, and subject to audit; unauthorized use is prohibited and subject to criminal and civil penalties; and use of the system indicates consent to monitoring and recording. [NIST AC-8 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-8 AE Mandatory]

4.3. The system use notification shall state that users are accessing a U.S. Government system. [NIST AC-8 Low/Moderate/High]

4.4. The system use notification shall state that users are accessing a system that contains U.S. Government information. [ARC-AMPE AC-8 AE Mandatory]

4.5. The organization shall retain the notification message or banner on the screen until users acknowledge the usage conditions and take explicit actions to log on to or further access the system. [NIST AC-8 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-8 AE Mandatory]

4.6. For publicly accessible systems, the organization shall: display system use information under [Assignment: organization-defined conditions] before granting further access; display references, if any, to monitoring, recording, or auditing consistent with privacy accommodations for such systems that generally prohibit those activities; and include a description of the authorized uses of the system. [NIST AC-8 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-8 AE Mandatory]

## 5. Session Control

5.1. The organization shall limit the number of concurrent sessions for each [Assignment: organization-defined account and/or account types] to [Assignment: organization-defined number]. [NIST AC-10 High]

5.2. The number of concurrent sessions for each account and/or account type shall be limited to one (1) session; any requirement for more than one concurrent session must be expressly required for the performance of job duties and documented in the applicable security and privacy plan. [ARC-AMPE AC-10 AE Mandatory]

5.3. The organization shall prevent further access to the system by initiating a device lock after [Assignment: organization-defined time period] of inactivity and/or requiring the user to initiate a device lock before leaving the system unattended. [NIST AC-11 Moderate/High]

5.4. Further access to the system shall be prevented by initiating a device lock after fifteen (15) minutes of inactivity (covering both remote and internal access connections) and by requiring the user to initiate a device lock before leaving the system unattended. [ARC-AMPE AC-11 AE Mandatory]

5.5. The device lock shall be retained until the user reestablishes access using established identification and authentication procedures. [NIST AC-11 Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-11 AE Mandatory]

5.6. The organization shall conceal, via the device lock, information previously visible on the display with a publicly viewable image. [NIST AC-11(1) Moderate/High]

5.7. The organization shall implement policies and procedures that specify the proper functions to be performed, the manner in which those functions are to be performed, and the physical attributes of the surroundings of a specific workstation or class of workstation that can access electronic protected health information. [HIPAA 164.310(b)]

5.8. The organization shall automatically terminate a user session after [Assignment: organization-defined conditions or trigger events]. [NIST AC-12 Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-12 AE Mandatory]

5.9. The organization shall provide a logout capability for user-initiated communications sessions whenever authentication is used to gain access to [Assignment: organization-defined information resources]; for ARC-AMPE, the information resources must be defined in the applicable security and privacy plans. [NIST AC-12(1) | ARC-AMPE AC-12(1) AE Mandatory]

5.10. The organization shall display an explicit logout message to users indicating the termination of authenticated communications sessions; for ARC-AMPE, an organization-defined standard logout message must be documented in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan (e.g., "Your session has been terminated"). [NIST AC-12(2) | ARC-AMPE AC-12(2) AE Mandatory]

5.11. The organization shall display an explicit message to users indicating that the session will end in [Assignment: organization-defined time]; for ARC-AMPE, the time until end of session must be specified in the applicable security and privacy plans. [NIST AC-12(3) | ARC-AMPE AC-12(3) AE Mandatory]

5.12. The organization shall implement electronic procedures that terminate an electronic session after a predetermined time of inactivity. [HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iii) Addressable]

## 6. Access Control and Identity Baseline (HIPAA)

6.1. The organization shall implement technical policies and procedures for electronic information systems that maintain electronic protected health information to allow access only to those persons or software programs that have been granted access rights as specified in § 164.308(a)(4). [HIPAA 164.312(a)(1)]

6.2. The organization shall assign a unique name and/or number for identifying and tracking user identity. [HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(i) Required]

6.3. The organization shall establish (and implement as needed) procedures for obtaining necessary electronic protected health information during an emergency. [HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(ii) Required]

6.4. The organization shall implement a mechanism to encrypt and decrypt electronic protected health information. [HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv) Addressable]

6.5. The organization shall implement procedures to verify that a person or entity seeking access to electronic protected health information is the one claimed. [HIPAA 164.312(d)]

## 7. Identification and Authentication Policy and Procedures

7.1. The organization shall develop, document, and disseminate to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] an identification and authentication policy (addressing purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines) and procedures to facilitate implementation of the policy and associated controls. [NIST IA-1 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-1 AE Mandatory]

7.2. The organization shall designate an [Assignment: organization-defined official] to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the identification and authentication policy and procedures. [NIST IA-1 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-1 AE Mandatory]

7.3. The organization shall review and update the current identification and authentication policy and procedures [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events]. [NIST IA-1 Low/Moderate/High]

7.4. The identification and authentication policy and procedures shall be reviewed and updated at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events (such as assessment or audit findings; security or privacy incidents; and changes to applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines). [ARC-AMPE IA-1 AE Mandatory]

IAM Engineering shall perform the reviews required by 7.3 and 7.4 and shall retain the resulting Authentication policy configuration export as evidence of the configured state.

7.5. The organization shall maintain the policies and procedures implemented to comply with the HIPAA Security Rule in written (which may be electronic) form, and shall maintain a written (which may be electronic) record of any action, activity, or assessment required to be documented. [HIPAA 164.316(b)(1)]

7.6. Required documentation shall be retained for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date when it last was in effect, whichever is later. [HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(i) Required]

7.7. Documentation shall be made available to those persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which the documentation pertains. [HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(ii) Required]

7.8. Documentation shall be reviewed periodically and updated as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of the electronic protected health information. [HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(iii) Required]

## 8. User Identification and Authentication

8.1. The organization shall uniquely identify and authenticate organizational users and associate that unique identification with processes acting on behalf of those users. [NIST IA-2 Low/Moderate/High | FedRAMP IA-2 | ARC-AMPE IA-2 AE Mandatory]

8.2. The organization shall employ effective identity proofing and authentication processes compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63 Digital Identity Guidelines document suite, and shall require the use of system and/or network authenticators and unique user identifiers for organizational users; help desk support requires user identification for any transaction with information security and privacy implications. [ARC-AMPE IA-2 AE Mandatory]

8.3. The organization shall implement multi-factor authentication for access to privileged accounts. [NIST IA-2(1) Low/Moderate/High | FedRAMP IA-2(1) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(1) AE Mandatory]

8.4. Multi-factor authentication must be phishing-resistant, in accordance with current CISA guidance. [FedRAMP IA-2(1) | FedRAMP IA-2(2)]

8.5. The organization shall implement multi-factor authentication for access to non-privileged accounts. [NIST IA-2(2) Low/Moderate/High | FedRAMP IA-2(2) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(2) AE Mandatory]

8.6. For non-privileged accounts, multi-factor authentication is required for all non-consumer account types; while MFA is not currently mandated for consumer accounts, it is strongly recommended. [ARC-AMPE IA-2(2) AE Mandatory]

IAM Engineering shall produce the MFA enrolment report on a continuous basis as evidence of multi-factor authentication enrolment under 8.3 through 8.6.

8.7. When shared accounts or authenticators are employed, the organization shall require users to be individually authenticated before granting access to the shared accounts or resources. [NIST IA-2(5) High | ARC-AMPE IA-2(5) AE Mandatory]

8.8. For multi-factor authentication to local, network, and remote access to privileged and non-privileged accounts, one of the factors must be provided by a device separate from the system gaining access, and that device must meet [Assignment: organization-defined strength of mechanism requirements]. [NIST IA-2(6) | FedRAMP IA-2(6)]

8.9. For multi-factor authentication to local, network, and remote access to privileged and non-privileged accounts, one of the factors must be provided by a device separate from the system gaining access, and that device must meet the latest published FIPS 140-compliant cryptography. [ARC-AMPE IA-2(6) AE Mandatory]

8.10. The organization shall implement replay-resistant authentication mechanisms for access to privileged and non-privileged accounts. [NIST IA-2(8) Low/Moderate/High | FedRAMP IA-2(8) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(8) AE Mandatory]

8.11. The organization shall provide a single sign-on capability for [Assignment: organization-defined system accounts and services]. [NIST IA-2(10)]

8.12. The organization shall accept and electronically verify Personal Identity Verification-compliant credentials. [NIST IA-2(12) Low/Moderate/High]

8.13. The organization shall implement the following out-of-band authentication mechanisms under \[Assignment: organization-defined conditions\]: [Assignment: organization-defined out-of-band authentication]. [NIST IA-2(13)]

## 9. Device Identification and Authentication

9.1. The organization shall uniquely identify and authenticate [Assignment: organization-defined devices and/or types of devices] before establishing a [Selection (one or more): local; remote; network] connection. [NIST IA-3 Moderate/High]

9.2. The organization shall uniquely identify and authenticate devices that require authentication mechanisms before establishing a local, remote, or network connection, using at minimum shared information (MAC or IP address) and access control lists to control remote network access; the specific devices and/or device types approved for identification and authentication management must be defined in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan. [ARC-AMPE IA-3 AE Mandatory]

9.3. The organization shall authenticate [Assignment: organization-defined devices and/or types of devices] before establishing a [Selection (one or more): local; remote; network] connection using bidirectional authentication that is cryptographically based. [NIST IA-3(1)]

9.4. Where addresses are allocated dynamically, the organization shall standardize dynamic address allocation lease information and lease duration in accordance with [Assignment: organization-defined lease information and lease duration], and shall audit lease information when assigned to a device. [NIST IA-3(3)]

9.5. The organization shall handle device identification and authentication based on attestation by [Assignment: organization-defined configuration management process]. [NIST IA-3(4)]

## 10. Authenticator Management

10.1. The organization shall manage system authenticators by: verifying, as part of initial authenticator distribution, the identity of the individual, group, role, service, or device receiving the authenticator; establishing initial authenticator content for any authenticators issued by the organization; ensuring authenticators have sufficient strength of mechanism for their intended use; establishing and implementing administrative procedures for initial authenticator distribution, for lost, compromised, or damaged authenticators, and for revoking authenticators; changing default authenticators prior to first use; protecting authenticator content from unauthorized disclosure and modification; requiring individuals to take, and having devices implement, specific controls to protect authenticators; and changing authenticators for group or role accounts when membership to those accounts changes. [NIST IA-5 Low/Moderate/High | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

10.2. The organization shall change or refresh authenticators [Assignment: organization-defined time period by authenticator type] or when [Assignment: organization-defined events] occur. [NIST IA-5 Low/Moderate/High | FedRAMP IA-5]

10.3. Authenticators shall be changed or refreshed immediately when they are no longer valid due to known or suspected compromise, and immediately upon system installation (e.g., default or vendor-supplied passwords). [ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

10.4. Authenticators must be compliant with the most recent NIST Digital Identity Guidelines at IAL, AAL, and FAL level 1 for Certification Class B, level 2 for Certification Class C, and level 3 for Certification Class D. [FedRAMP IA-5]

10.5. The organization shall encrypt authentication assertions when passed through third parties, such as a browser (e.g., a SAML assertion encrypted using XML-Encryption, or an OpenID Connect ID Token encrypted using JSON Web Encryption). [FedRAMP IA-5]

10.6. The organization shall comply with the latest published NIST SP 800-63B for authenticator management; Organizational System/User Account passwords shall be paired with multi-factor authentication (strongly recommended for Organizational ACA Consumer Account passwords), and it is strongly recommended to enforce a policy requiring Organizational System/User Account passwords be changed or refreshed at least once every six (6) months. [ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

### 10.1. Password Requirements

10.7. The organization shall maintain a list of commonly-used, expected, or compromised passwords and shall update the list [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and when organizational passwords are suspected to have been compromised directly or indirectly. [NIST IA-5(1) Low/Moderate/High]

10.8. The organization shall maintain a list of commonly used, expected, or compromised passwords and shall update it using a frequency defined in applicable security/privacy plans, not to exceed one (1) year, and when organizational passwords are suspected to have been compromised directly or indirectly. [ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

10.9. When users create or update passwords, the organization shall verify that the passwords are not found on the list of commonly-used, expected, or compromised passwords. [NIST IA-5(1) Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

10.10. Passwords shall be transmitted only over cryptographically-protected channels. [NIST IA-5(1) Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

10.11. Passwords shall be stored using an approved salted key derivation function, preferably using a keyed hash. [NIST IA-5(1) Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

10.12. The organization shall require immediate selection of a new password upon account recovery. [NIST IA-5(1) Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

10.13. The organization shall allow user selection of long passwords and passphrases, including spaces and all printable characters. [NIST IA-5(1) Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

10.14. The organization shall employ automated tools to assist the user in selecting strong password authenticators. [NIST IA-5(1) Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

10.15. The organization shall enforce password composition and complexity rules of [Assignment: organization-defined composition and complexity rules]. [NIST IA-5(1) Low/Moderate/High]

10.16. Password composition and complexity shall comply with the latest published NIST SP 800-63B, with a minimum of eight (8) characters for ACA Consumer Accounts and all other accounts, and a minimum of twelve (12) characters for Administrator/Privileged Accounts; dictionary words must not be used as passwords, use of passphrases is strongly recommended, temporary passwords should trigger an immediate change to a permanent password, and mobile devices may be excluded from the complexity requirement depending on organizational risk tolerance. [ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

### 10.2. Public Key and PKI Requirements

10.17. For public key-based authentication, the organization shall enforce authorized access to the corresponding private key, and shall map the authenticated identity to the account of the individual or group; and when PKI is used, the organization shall validate certificates by constructing and verifying a certification path to an accepted trust anchor, including checking certificate status information, and shall implement a local cache of revocation data to support path discovery and validation. [NIST IA-5(2) Moderate/High]

10.18. The organization shall require developers and installers of system components to provide unique authenticators or change default authenticators prior to delivery and installation. [NIST IA-5(5)]

### 10.3. Authenticator Protection

10.19. The organization shall protect authenticators commensurate with the security category of the information to which use of the authenticator permits access. [NIST IA-5(6) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(6) AE Mandatory]

10.20. The organization shall ensure that unencrypted static authenticators are not embedded in applications or other forms of static storage. [NIST IA-5(7) | ARC-AMPE IA-5(7) AE Mandatory]

10.21. The organization shall implement [Assignment: organization-defined security controls] to manage the risk of compromise due to individuals having accounts on multiple systems. [NIST IA-5(8)]

10.22. The organization shall prohibit the use of cached authenticators after [Assignment: organization-defined time period]. [NIST IA-5(13)]

10.23. The organization shall employ [Assignment: organization-defined password managers] to generate and manage passwords, and shall protect the passwords using [Assignment: organization-defined controls]. [NIST IA-5(18)]

### 10.4. Specialized Authenticator Requirements

10.24. The organization shall use the following external organizations to federate credentials: [Assignment: organization-defined external organizations]. [NIST IA-5(9)]

10.25. The organization shall bind identities and authenticators dynamically using the following rules: [Assignment: organization-defined binding rules]. [NIST IA-5(10)]

10.26. For biometric-based authentication, the organization shall employ mechanisms that satisfy [Assignment: organization-defined biometric quality requirements]. [NIST IA-5(12)]

10.27. For PKI-based authentication, the organization shall employ an organization-wide methodology for managing the content of PKI trust stores installed across all platforms, including networks, operating systems, browsers, and applications. [NIST IA-5(14)]

10.28. The organization shall use only General Services Administration-approved products and services for identity, credential, and access management. [NIST IA-5(15)]

10.29. The organization shall require that the issuance of [Assignment: organization-defined types of and/or specific authenticators] be conducted [Selection: in person; by a trusted external party] before [Assignment: organization-defined registration authority] with authorization by [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles]. [NIST IA-5(16)]

10.30. The organization shall employ presentation attack detection mechanisms for biometric-based authentication. [NIST IA-5(17)]

## 11. Authentication Feedback

11.1. The organization shall obscure feedback of authentication information during the authentication process to protect the information from possible exploitation and use by unauthorized individuals. [NIST IA-6 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-6 AE Mandatory]

## 12. Cryptographic Module Authentication

12.1. The organization shall implement mechanisms for authentication to a cryptographic module that meet the requirements of applicable laws, executive orders, directives, policies, regulations, standards, and guidelines for such authentication. [NIST IA-7 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-7 AE Mandatory]

12.2. Information systems containing Personally Identifiable Information (PII) must use the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standards. [ARC-AMPE IA-7 AE Mandatory]

## 13. Non-Organizational User Authentication

13.1. The organization shall uniquely identify and authenticate non-organizational users or processes acting on behalf of non-organizational users. [NIST IA-8 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-8 AE Mandatory]

13.2. The organization shall employ effective identity proofing and authentication processes compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63 Digital Identity Guidelines at IAL-2/AAL-2, shall require the use of system and/or network authenticators and unique user identifiers for non-organizational users, and shall require user identification for help desk support transactions with information security and privacy implications. [ARC-AMPE IA-8 AE Mandatory]

13.3. The organization shall accept and electronically verify Personal Identity Verification-compliant credentials from other federal agencies. [NIST IA-8(1) Low/Moderate/High]

13.4. The organization shall accept only external authenticators that are NIST-compliant, and shall document and maintain a list of accepted external authenticators. [NIST IA-8(2) Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-8(2) AE Mandatory]

13.5. External credentials must be certified as compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63 Digital Identity Guidelines document suite by an approved accreditation authority, must meet or exceed those guidelines, and the organization must use General Services Administration-approved products and services for identity, credential, and access management. [ARC-AMPE IA-8(2) AE Mandatory]

13.6. The organization shall conform to [Assignment: organization-defined identity management profiles] for identity management. [NIST IA-8(4) Low/Moderate/High]

13.7. The organization shall conform to organization-defined profiles for identity management, defined using identity proofing and authentication processes compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63 Digital Identity Guidelines document suite. [ARC-AMPE IA-8(4) AE Mandatory]

13.8. The organization shall accept and verify federated or PKI credentials that meet [Assignment: organization-defined policy]. [NIST IA-8(5)]

13.9. The organization shall implement the following measures to disassociate user attributes or identifier assertion relationships among individuals, credential service providers, and relying parties: [Assignment: organization-defined measures]. [NIST IA-8(6)]

## 14. Re-authentication

14.1. The organization shall require users to re-authenticate when [Assignment: organization-defined circumstances or situations] occur, such as when authenticators, credentials, or roles change; when security categories of systems change; when execution of privileged functions occurs; or after a fixed time period; for ARC-AMPE, these circumstances must be defined in the applicable security/privacy plans. [NIST IA-11 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-11 AE Mandatory]

## 15. Evidence and Records

IAM Engineering shall produce and retain the following evidence on a continuous basis:

| Artifact                                   | Purpose                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| MFA enrolment report                       | Evidence of multi-factor authentication enrolment for privileged and non-privileged accounts (Sections 8.3–8.6)                      |
| Authentication policy configuration export | Evidence of the configured authentication policy state, including lockout, session, and password settings (Sections 3, 5, 7, and 10) |

Documentation maintained under this Standard, including HIPAA Security Rule policies, procedures, and records of required actions, activities, and assessments, shall be retained in written (which may be electronic) form for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date when it last was in effect, whichever is later, and shall be made available to those persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which it pertains.
